subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. GenServe vs CloudIA - HelixHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs GenServe vs CloudIA

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned.

High-level pain points you called out:
- 95th-pct inference latency currently ~180ms across peak workloads (goal: <150ms)
- Unit cost too high for high-volume indexing / vector generation (target: ~30% cost reduction)
- Need VPC/private deployment + KMS/HSM support for PHI-handling flows
- Multi-region routing for lower tail latency and DR

Goals for a successful vendor:
1) Demonstrable 95th-pct latency <150ms on your anonymized patient-note workload
2) Predictable throughput at 500 qps with autoscaling and buffer for bursts
3) Clear TCO (including quantization / batching tradeoffs) and procurement-friendly pricing
4) SOC 2 + evidence of KMS/HSM integration for key management

Competitive landscape you’re evaluating: GenServe (on-prem hybrid), CloudIA (managed), and Redwood.

Decision criteria (based on call):
- Latency/throughput under representative workload
- Cost per 1,000 requests and expected savings with batching/quantization
- Private deployment / VPC & key management compatibility
- Observability / debugging (per-route tracing, token-level cost)
- Rollout controls & fallbacks

Open questions we captured:
- Baseline dataset for tests (you mentioned a sample set)
- Region constraints (where test infra should live)
- Procurement/POC legal contacts and NDA needs
- Specific test duration and pass/fail criteria for each scenario

Proposed next steps (we’ll do this unless you prefer changes):
1) Redwood will run a 48-hour targeted bake-off starting next week covering three scenarios: latency-only, throughput under burst, and private-deploy smoke test.
2) We’ll run tests in us-east-1 (unless you confirm otherwise) and deliver a benchmark spreadsheet with latency percentiles, token costs, and config used.
3) Technical kickoff: Rishi + your engineering lead to confirm test access and sample dataset.
4) Business: we’ll provide a side-by-side competitive brief and a short TCO model.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-brief.pdf, proposed-test-plan.xlsx

Proposed meeting for results review: Wed Mar 15, 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications and confirmations from our side:

1) Dataset: we’ll provide a ~10k-sample subset of our patient-note dataset (anonymized) — link will be shared by EOD Monday. Use the set labeled "patient-note-sim v2" as the baseline.
2) Region: please run the tests in us-east-1 — we need to minimize egress and ensure latency numbers reflect our primary region.
3) Compliance: we need KMS/HSM details and a SOC 2 artifact we can share with procurement. If you can attach SOC 2 cert excerpt and KMS architecture/diagram to the bake-off results that’ll speed procurement.
4) Competitor baseline: FYI, our internal tests with GenServe showed ~180ms 95th-pct under the same sample; we expect vendors to be compared against that baseline.

Procurement & legal: please add Priya Mehta (procurement) to future threads: priya.mehta@helixhealth.com — she’ll own the POC paperwork.

We’re good to proceed with the 48-hour POC. Kickoff can be Tue 13 Mar in the morning PT.
